note: Inkwell's always-true list, in check 3's format. This is the worked example for the format, and it is also the artifact `inspector examine --always-true` reads: one name, one file, one check. It replaces the earlier hand-written prose list, whose five invariants are all carried below. Three lines deliberately carry no falsifier and say why in their own note - a promise nothing can currently disprove is reported as not-runnable and never as passing, which is the state Inkwell's list is honestly in today.

promises.promise: An inkling is never lost once captured: a record the backend accepted is readable afterwards, with the text it was captured with.
promises.source: named on inspector#24; the earlier prose list stated it as the upsert property

promises.promise: A delete removes both the markdown file and its audio sibling, leaving neither behind.
promises.note: No falsifier yet, so this line is reported as not-runnable rather than passing. Two reasons, both about the observation surface rather than about Inkwell: the feature map documents no delete endpoint, and the backend's storage effects are outside the HTTP surface check 3 can observe. A command falsifier in a runner image that can read the app's storage directory is what would make this runnable.

promises.promise: An inkling captured but not yet synced survives a restart of the app that holds it.
promises.note: No falsifier yet, so this line is reported as not-runnable rather than passing. It is a property of the native client's local store, which this format drives nothing of, and check 3 brings one app instance up per run rather than restarting it mid-list.

promises.promise: GET /inklings returns its records ordered by newest created timestamp first.
promises.source: carried over from the earlier hand-written prose always-true list
promises.note: No falsifier yet, so this line is reported as not-runnable rather than passing. An http falsifier's expectations are status and substring, which cannot express an ordering between two records; this needs a command falsifier in a runner image that can read the JSON.
